text:
maya: FYI CI on infra/gke-provision is flaking hard — matrix jobs fail with cache-restore timeouts, then terraform apply sits waiting for state lock and helm-sync ends up timing out because nodes never become Ready. Anyone seen this combo today?
eng-ci-bot: gha run #3456 (branch: gke-provision) — failure summary: restore-cache timeout (60s), job 'provision-gpu' aborted, terraform apply: error acquiring state lock (409), helm sync: timeout waiting for pods. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/3456 
Samir: can you paste the relevant log snippets? looks like either cache backend or runner preemption is corrupting state writes.
maya: snippets: ```
Restore cache action: timed out after 60s, response 200 but empty body
error acquiring state lock: resource busy (conflict)
waiting for lock (10m)
helm: failed waiting for rollout: pods not ready (node not ready)
```
olivia: do we have concurrency groups mixing across branches? a mis-scoped concurrency can cause multiple applies to race for the same remote state key. try: ```
concurrency:
  group: infra-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
devops-oncall: we already have `concurrency` but the group key is `infra-main` for PR builds due to a template bug — so PRs and main runs are sharing a lock. also seeing intermittent GCS 503s during cache upload which leaves partial archives.
Samir: that explains partial restores -> terraform runs with stale state and then hits lock. quick mitigations: 1) make concurrency group per-ref (olivia's snippet) 2) add a cleanup step to `terraform apply` that force-unlocks a stale lock after verifying no active apply 3) increase cache restore retries and validate checksum after restore.
maya: also, at ~10:42 we hit GPU quota exhaustion in us-west1, so terraform retried to us-central which triggered node pool creation in a different region and significantly delayed readiness — that caused helm timeouts. quota spike coincides with other customers scaling.
olivia: short-term add a pre-helm readiness gate: `kubectl wait --for=condition=ready pod -l app=kube-provision --timeout=5m` before running `helm upgrade --install`. also switch heavier cache artifacts to actions/cache v3 with retry/backoff or upload artifacts to our s3 fallback.
Samir: I'll open a tiny PR to scope concurrency correctly + add a `post` step: ```
- name: Force-unlock stale TF lock
  if: failure()
  run: |
    LOCK_ID=$(cat .tfstate.lock) || true
    if [ -n "$LOCK_ID" ]; then terraform force-unlock -force $LOCK_ID || true; fi
```
devops-oncall: FYI preemptions are still causing partial writes; ops will add a short-lived retry proxy for cache uploads today. also increasing GPU quota request for us-west1 to handle bursts next week (cost impact noted).
maya: what's the rough cost hit from retries yesterday?
Samir: ballpark >$400 across failed provisioning retries and ephemeral node hours. not huge but worth fixing to avoid repeated churn.
eng-ci-bot: related runs: https://ci.internal/runs/3456, https://ci.internal/runs/3460, https://ci.internal/runs/3472 — all show similar cache/lock + node-not-ready stacks.
maya: ok thanks — sounds like action items: samir PR for concurrency + unlock, olivia add readiness gate + cache retry, devops-oncall add s3 fallback proxy and quota request. I'll monitor after PRs merge.
Samir: on it, will tag you in the PR and add a short changelog. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — appreciate the quick response :eyes:
